blocks.text:
At 07:00, depart by speedboat for Isabela. The crossing takes around 2 hours. On arrival in Puerto Villamil, you will head to the wetlands.

Different species of mangroves grow here, with small lagoons among volcanic formations and birds including flamingos and black-necked stilts. This walk reveals another side of the island: dry lava fields give way to wetlands, shallow water and birds feeding beside the lagoons. Your next stop is the information centre, where you will learn about the work of Galápagos National Park and its programmes to conserve local flora and fauna.

After lunch at a local restaurant, the group will head to Tintoreras, an islet south of Puerto Villamil. In the turquoise bay, you may see sea lions, sea turtles, marine iguanas and rays. Tintoreras is also known as a resting place for reef sharks, which you can see after a short walk over solidified lava. Water, black volcanic rock and the animals that draw many visitors to the archipelago come together in this small area.

Return to Puerto Ayora at around 17:00. The evening is free.

**Accommodation:** Lobo de Mar 3*.  
**Meals:** breakfast, lunch.
